predecessors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
predecessors.text: 54 cells of Roman Palaestina Tertia (the Negev, Sinai and the Arabah, 34.6-36.4 E, 28.1-31.3 N) that the Ghassanid shape of 510 takes from the Eastern Roman shape of 509

successors.name: Rashidun Caliphate
successors.text: the Ghassanid country: Cliopatria's Rashidun shape of 634 contains 945 of its 946 cells

ledger.x: 510: the Ghassanids appear on Rome's Arab frontier.
510: the Ghassanid shape reaches into Roman Palaestina Tertia.
617 (Cliopatria's year): the Syrian desert north of the Hejaz passes to the Persians.
617 (Cliopatria's year): the remainder of the Ghassanid country, in the north-west of Arabia, drops out of every shape to 628.
617 (Cliopatria's year): the Roman client relation is broken by the Persian occupation.
629: the rest of the Ghassanid country is drawn again (Cliopatria's year); no page dates a restoration there.
629 (Cliopatria's year): the client relation resumes with the return of the territories.
633: hand-over between two dossiers of one continuous state.

633: the same client relation, now with the Byzantine Empire row of Cliopatria (one continuous state with the Eastern Roman Empire, see the previous event). byzantine-empire /ledger/1 ends the tint in 633 without a start; it should read vassal_start 633 and vassal_end 636 (request to eu-05).
634 (24 April): the Muslims attack the Ghassanids.
636: the Yarmuk ends the fight for the frontier.
636: the Ghassanid country passes to the Muslims.
636: the Ghassanid client kingdom is lost.
636: the Ghassanids lose their country at the Yarmuk.

wars.name: Ghassanid-Lakhmid wars
wars.outcome: A grazing-rights dispute with Mundhir near Palmyra in 537/538 or 539; at Yawm Halima near Chalcis in June 554 the Lakhmids were defeated and Mundhir fell, but Harith lost his eldest son Jabalah; in 575 Mundhir ibn al-Harith struck Hira, which 'was sacked…

wars.name: Ghassanid revolt after the arrest of al-Mundhir
wars.outcome: Maurice accused Mundhir of treason after the failed campaign towards Ctesiphon; the arrest sparked a revolt by his sons, especially al-Nu'man, who raided Byzantine provinces for about two years; the Byzantines broke up the Ghassanid confederation in 584.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628
wars.outcome: Damascus, Apamea and Emesa fell to the Persians in 613, Jerusalem in 614; the peace of 628-629 gave back all lost territories.

wars.name: Battle of Mu'tah
wars.outcome: 'The Battle of Mu'tah was fought in September 629 near the village of Mu'tah' and 'the Muslim army was routed'; the Levant page gives as the cause that 'a Ghassanid official executed Muhammad's emissary who was en route to Bosra'.

wars.name: Rashidun conquest of Syria
wars.outcome: First invasion in late 633-early 634 (Khalid's attack on pro-Byzantine Ghassanids on 24 April 634); Bosra in May 634, Fahl in December 634 or January 635, Damascus in August or September 635, Homs in December 635 or January 636, Yarmuk in 636, which 'sealed…

certainty.note: A steppe and desert frontier of client Arabs, drawn as a zone: no border is fixed by treaty or survey on the pages opened; the edge against the Roman provinces is the softest.
